outcome: minimum ST elevation in lead V2
intimal flap (mid left anterior descending artery) spontaneous dissection with subintimal hematoma
cohort: A 37-year-old female with a history of hypertension, systemic lupus erythematosus, preeclampsia with 3 cesarean deliveries, and an active smoking habit, who presented with chest pain.
finding: This case highlights the challenge of early diagnosis of Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection (SCAD) and emphasizes its association with autoimmune diseases, specifically Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE).
mod_finding: The patient had a history of 3 cesarean deliveries along with preeclampsia, which are noted as part of her complex medical history relevant to SCAD risk.
